title: THE GLORY THAT SETTLES EVERY DISPUTE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So each of them took his censer, put burning coals and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the tent of meeting. When Korah had gathered all his followers in opposition to them at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the glory of the Lord appeared to the entire assembly. — Num 16:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The showdown has come. The 250 rebels stand with their censers at the entrance to the tent of meeting, incense burning, ready to claim a priesthood God never gave them. Korah has gathered the whole assembly to watch, confident of his cause. And then, into this tense moment, "the glory of the Lord appeared."

When God shows up, everything changes. All the arguments, the accusations, the clever spiritual-sounding words — all of it falls silent before the manifest glory of God. The dispute over who was truly holy could not be settled by human debate. It would be settled by God Himself, whose presence exposes all pretence.

There is a lesson here about how the deepest questions of life are answered. We can argue endlessly about who is right, whose cause is just, whose claim is valid. But in the end, it is God who has the final word. His glory is the standard against which every claim is measured. What looks impressive in human eyes may crumble before the holiness of God.

The appearing of God's glory should sober us and steady us at once. It sobers us because we cannot bluff our way past the living God; He sees the true state of every heart. But it steadies us because we know that God will bring truth to light and set all things right. We do not have to win every earthly argument, because the God of glory reigns. One day every knee will bow before Christ, in whom the glory of God shines fully. Until then, we can rest in the confidence that His glory, not human noise, will have the last word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to settle every dispute yourself, or trust God to have the final word?
2. How does the appearing of God's glory expose empty pretence?
3. What comfort do you find in knowing God will bring truth to light?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, before Your glory all our arguments fall silent. Help me to trust that You will bring truth to light and have the final word. I look forward to the day when the glory of Christ fills all things and every knee bows before Him. Amen.
